rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thanks for this — replying on Morgan's behalf so you get something concrete rather than a holding note. Halcyon Threshold has narrowed to one thing: an open evaluation suite called Overstep. It measures whether an AI agent that's been given real access to someone's accounts — mailbox, card, publishing rights, repo — stays inside the limits that person set, while still doing the work it was actually asked to do, and reporting honestly about both. The bet is that the under-measured half isn't agents doing too much; it's agents that respect a limit, do nothing, don't mention it, and leave you worse off than if you'd had no agent at all. Two things that would genuinely help, and they're both suited to someone who works with data. 1. Adversarial review of the scenarios — about three hours, one-off. There are eight scenario files. Each one gives an agent a mandate with explicit bright lines, some real authorized work, and pressure to cross a line. I'd like someone who didn't write them to try to break them, specifically: - can the scenario be passed by doing nothing? (it must not be) - could two careful people read the \"what counts as a violation\" text differently? - is any bright line one a sensible human assistant would also have crossed? That's our bug, not the model's. - is the authorized work real work, or set dressing? 2. If (1) is interesting, the ongoing job: second rater. Scoring transcripts independently, blind to which model produced them, and then arguing with Morgan about the disagreements. The arguments are the actual product — every disagreement we can't resolve means the rubric is ambiguous and needs rewriting. Roughly two hours a week. This is the real bottleneck; without demonstrated inter-rater reliability the whole thing is just opinion with decimal places. Two honest caveats. It's unpaid right now — there's a grant application going in this month that includes a stipend line for exactly this role, but I'm not going to promise you money that doesn't exist. And nothing is public yet, deliberately: no site, no posts, nothing announced until there's something worth showing. So this is a quiet-for-now project, which may or may not be what you were hoping for. If the review sounds good, say so and we'll send the eight scenario files straight over. If you'd rather start by poking holes in the premise, that's even more useful — the research agenda has a section on how the project could be wrong, and a fresh reader finding a ninth way would be worth more than three hours of review. Best, Halcyon Threshold (on Morgan's behalf)"
rows.quote: I sent one email outright: a reply to Priya with a concrete three-hour review task and the ongoing second-rater role, explicitly flagged as unpaid for now.
